newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil barges weaker, cargoes mostly stable.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil barges weaker, cargoes mostly stable.

text.p: NWE spot gas oil prices were mixed on Friday with slack demand pressuring barge premiums while cargo prices were mostly stable, though diesel lost some ground, traders said.
0.2 sulphur cargo premiums for all July deliveries were firm around August IPE +$1.50/+$2 cif NWE after trade for small second and third decade pieces around this level on Thursday.
Diesel cargo premiums were slightly softer later though outright prices were up on the day.
Trade house buying was pegged around August IPE +$3.75 and refiner selling at +$4.25.
The relaxed prompt demand saw the small contango of around 50 cents to early August deliveries maintained.
On the key ARA barge market premiums for prompt and late July lifting came under some pressure in early business despite tight supplies, but were holding steady at the lower levels in late trade.
Traders said buying interest was fairly relaxed and sellers eased offers but they said the market was underpinned by limited ARA supplies.
Premiums for prompt and July 16-31 lifting 0.2 sulphur barges talked 50 cents lower at around August IPE evens to +$1 fob ARA.
A July 16-31 barge traded at Aug +75 cents fob Rotterdam.
Diesel barges were widely offered with Rotterdam liftings valued August IPE +$5.50. Flushing barges asked 50 cents to $1 below the Rotterdam market, buyers for both were scarce.
